findings.title: Local cache entry set before the limit check lets rejected devices in on retry
findings.body: `tagDeviceUI` calls `localCache.SetDefault(key, ...)` before `CreateOrUpdateDevice`. If the store returns `ErrDeviceLimitReached`, the first request is rejected, but the cache key stays set. For the next ~29 minutes, `TagDevice` for that device returns nil from the cache hit, and `Authenticate` lets the request through. The device limit is effectively enforced only on a device's first request per cache window. The cache entry should be set only after a successful write, or removed when the write fails.

findings.title: Count-then-insert is not atomic, so concurrent devices can exceed the limit
findings.body: `CreateOrUpdateDevice` runs `CountDevices` and then the upsert as separate statements, with no transaction or lock. Several new devices arriving at the same time can all read `count < deviceLimit` and all insert. The configured limit can then be exceeded under load, and there is no later reconciliation.

findings.title: RowsAffected==0 is treated as limit reached, which misfires on MySQL no-op updates
findings.body: Once the limit is reached, `updateDevice` returns `ErrDeviceLimitReached` whenever `RowsAffected()` is 0. By default MySQL reports only rows whose values actually changed. `updated_at` has second precision, so a repeat update for an existing device in the same second with the same IP and user agent reports 0 rows. That registered, legitimate device is then rejected as over the limit. The update should check that the device exists rather than relying on rows changed (or use CLIENT_FOUND_ROWS).

findings.title: Device tagging moved onto the synchronous auth path
findings.body: `TagDevice` used to run in a background goroutine with its own timeout. It now runs inline in `Authenticate` using the request context. On a cache miss it does a COUNT query plus an upsert or update on the request path, which adds DB latency to anonymous requests. A slow DB, or a request context that is cancelled, now directly delays or affects authentication. The panic recovery from the goroutine version was also removed.

findings.title: ProvideAnonDBStore signature change may break the wire provider set
findings.body: `ProvideAnonDBStore` now takes a `deviceLimit int64`, and `ProvideAnonymousDeviceService` builds the store itself. If the wire provider sets (wire.go / wireexts) still register `anonstore.ProvideAnonDBStore` and bind `AnonStore`, injector generation will fail. Either no int64 provider exists, or the provider is now unused. Those wire files are not updated in this PR.

findings.title: Raw store error returned to the auth broker when the limit is reached
findings.body: `Authenticate` returns the plain `anonstore.ErrDeviceLimitReached` error, not an authn-specific error. The user probably gets a generic authentication failure with no clear message that the anonymous device limit was hit, and operators may struggle to diagnose why anonymous users are being rejected.

findings.title: 30-day expiration constant duplicated in several places
findings.body: `anonymousDeviceExpiration` is defined separately in `anonstore/database.go` and `api/api.go`, and `thirtyDays` remains in `impl.go`. These define the same counting window. If they drift apart, the device list, the usage stats and the limit enforcement would use different windows. Export a single constant from `anonstore` and use it everywhere.
